prompt: A flat coil of area $A$ is in a uniform field $B$, with its plane perpendicular to the field. The coil is rotated through $90^\circ$. What is the change in the magnitude of flux through it?
markscheme: **C.** The flux falls from $BA$ (field along the normal) to $0$ (field in the plane).

prompt: A simple generator produces an alternating emf of peak value $\varepsilon_0$ and period $T$. The coil is rotated at half the original speed. What are the new peak emf and period?

A metal rod of length $0.40\ \text{m}$ slides at a constant $3.0\ \text{m s}^{-1}$ along two horizontal rails connected by a $2.0\ \Omega$ resistor. A uniform vertical magnetic field of $0.50\ \text{T}$ acts across the rails. The rails and rod have negligible resistance.

**(a)** Explain, using Faraday’s law, why an emf is induced in the circuit. **[2]**

**(b)** Calculate the current in the resistor. **[2]**

**(c)** Determine the force needed to keep the rod moving at constant speed and show that the rate of work done by this force equals the power dissipated in the resistor. **[3]**
markscheme:
**(a)** As the rod moves, the area of the circuit inside the field increases ✓, so the flux linkage changes and an emf equal to its rate of change is induced ✓

**(b)** $\varepsilon = BvL = 0.50\times3.0\times0.40 = 0.60\ \text{V}$ ✓; $I = 0.60/2.0 = 0.30\ \text{A}$ ✓

**(c)** Magnetic force on the rod $F = BIL = 0.50\times0.30\times0.40 = 0.060\ \text{N}$, opposing the motion (Lenz), so an equal applied force is needed ✓; $P = Fv = 0.060\times3.0 = 0.18\ \text{W}$ ✓; $I^2R = 0.30^2\times2.0 = 0.18\ \text{W}$, the same ✓

prompt:
A bar magnet is dropped, north pole first, through a vertical coil connected to a data logger that records the induced emf.

**(a)** Describe and explain the shape of the emf–time graph as the magnet falls into and then out of the coil. **[3]**

**(b)** Explain why the magnet’s acceleration while passing through the coil is less than $g$ when the coil is connected to a resistor, but not when the coil is open-circuit. **[2]**
markscheme:
**(a)** A pulse of one sign as the magnet enters (flux increasing) ✓; the emf passes through zero when the magnet is in the middle and the flux is momentarily not changing ✓; a pulse of opposite sign and larger peak (but shorter duration) as it leaves, since flux decreases and the magnet is moving faster ✓

**(b)** With a closed circuit, an induced current flows whose magnetic field opposes the magnet’s motion (Lenz) — an upward force ✓; open-circuit, an emf is induced but no current flows, so there is no opposing force ✓
